world.b: North Korea test-fired two types of submarine-launched strategic cruise missiles off its east coast on Wednesday, state media KCNA reported.

world.h: Pope Leo's lung recovering well after surgery
world.b: Doctors said a chest X-ray showed good recovery and post-operative tests are normal; the Vatican said Leo has resumed working from the hospital.

world.h: Pakistan school roof collapse kills at least 29
world.b: The roof of a private school in Peshawar collapsed Thursday, killing at least 28 children and a teacher and injuring more than 50, officials said.

world.h: Ukraine strikes Russian refinery as truce ends
world.b: Ukrainian drones set a refinery in Russia's Ryazan region on fire early Thursday, hours after Zelenskyy said a brief truce spurned by Moscow was over.

world.h: Iran war: Strikes hit Houthis in Taiz
world.b: Al Jazeera's live coverage: strikes target Houthi positions in Taiz, and the Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted drones and missiles.
world.title: Strikes target Houthis in Taiz, coalition says intercepted drones, missiles

national.h: Teen gunman kills 4 at Oregon elementary school
national.b: A 16-year-old shot his way into Silver Rail Elementary in Bend, killing three children and a teacher, before being shot by a person who followed him inside, police said.

national.h: 5 believed dead in Oregon elementary school shooting
national.b: Officials told AP that five people are believed dead, including children, after a shooting at Silver Rail Elementary in Bend; police say the suspect is dead.

national.h: Fired FBI agents sue to get jobs back
national.b: Nine agents, analysts and staff fired after working on the Trump classified documents probe sued, calling their firings political retribution.

national.h: Suspicious letters sent to Senate, election offices
national.b: The FBI, Postal Inspection Service and Capitol Police are investigating letters with suspicious substances sent to congressional and election offices, treating them as potentially hazardous.

national.h: Some cut from ACA rolls are being added back
national.b: After the administration dropped 760,000 people from Affordable Care Act plans citing fraud, CMS has reinstated a small number whose coverage should not have been canceled, KFF Health News reports.

national.h: Abbott keeps Texas border emergency going
national.b: Texas Gov. Greg Abbott has renewed or amended his border disaster proclamation at least 69 times, 21 under Trump, even as the administration reports historic lows in crossings.
national.title: Trump Says the Border Is Secure. Texas Gov. Greg Abbott Keeps Declaring an Emergency.

national.h: OpenAI bugging suspect booked one-way flight
national.b: Prosecutors say former OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan, accused of bugging the company's headquarters, had booked a one-way flight to Saudi Arabia before his arrest.

politics.h: Press secretary Zacharia out after five days
politics.b: The White House says Katie Zacharia is "transitioning out." Trump had told her to "reconsider" staying and said there was no rush to name a replacement.
politics.title: White House press secretary Katie Zacharia fired after five days on the job

politics.b: The president is visiting battleground Georgia to boost GOP enthusiasm despite party divisions in the state.

politics.h: Talarico casts Texas Senate race as David vs. Goliath
politics.b: The Democrat told supporters "you are my slingshot" after Republicans invested more than $158 million against him.

politics.h: Court weighs who owns the president's papers
politics.b: Administration lawyers argue before a federal appeals court Friday that White House papers belong to Donald Trump, not the public, after the Justice Department moved to invalidate the Presidential Records Act.

politics.h: AP-NORC poll: Voters frustrated, want change
politics.b: Less than four weeks before Election Day, Democrats are more enthusiastic than Republicans and more voters want Democrats to control Congress.

politics.h: Wisconsin issues guidance on federal agents at polls
politics.b: The state elections commission sent clerks guidance on handling federal agents at polling places, over one Republican commissioner's objection.

politics.h: DOJ sues California over noncitizen mail ballots
politics.b: The Trump administration sued to block counting ballots from 20,000 people it says are likely noncitizens, after California missed a 48-hour deadline to review the list.

politics.h: Omar's phone seized, relatives subpoenaed: AP
politics.b: A Minnesota grand jury probing potential fraud in Rep. Ilhan Omar's immigration paperwork has subpoenaed relatives, and her phone was seized, AP reports.

politics.h: Missouri GOP targets how top judges are picked
politics.b: After court losses, Missouri Republicans want to change the merit-based Missouri Plan that has chosen the state's top judges since the 1940s, ProPublica reports.
politics.title: Frustrated by Losses in the Courts, Missouri Republicans Want to Change How Top Judges Are Selected

politics.h: Administration seeks to strip Omar's citizenship
politics.b: The Trump administration is investigating Rep. Ilhan Omar to revoke her citizenship and eventually deport her, the Wall Street Journal reported, with grand jury subpoenas issued to relatives.
At a rally in Bullhead City, Arizona, Trump said people who leak government information to the media should be shot.

international.h: Carney: outsiders "working to break" Canada
international.b: At a Calgary rally, the prime minister warned against Alberta's vote on whether to start a path toward a separation referendum.
international.title: Prime Minister Mark Carney says U.S. is trying to break Canada as Alberta votes on separation path

international.h: Russia strikes 9 Ukrainian regions
international.b: The attacks came amid fears that strained ties between Kyiv and Washington leave Ukraine more exposed to aerial assaults on its power grid before winter.
international.title: Russia strikes 9 Ukrainian regions as strain grows between Zelenskyy and Trump

international.h: Kenya records third Ebola case
international.b: A 65-year-old woman, a close relative of the first two cases, tested positive after being quarantined since Oct. 6, the Health Ministry said.
international.title: Kenya records third Ebola case, linked to first patient who died

international.h: Pope Leo to appear in public Sunday
international.b: The 71-year-old pope, who had part of his right lung removed Tuesday, can now carry out daily activities independently, his doctors said.
international.title: Pope Leo to make public appearance Sunday, first since cancer surgery

international.h: Settlers attack olive pickers, US journalist
international.b: Israeli settlers beat Palestinian olive pickers and a Washington Post photojournalist in the occupied West Bank and set olive groves ablaze.

international.h: Gaza starvation at 'catastrophic' levels
international.b: At least 466 Palestinians have died of malnutrition and starvation since 2024, a third of them children, the Gaza Health Ministry said on World Food Day.
international.title: Gaza malnutrition and starvation at ‘catastrophic’ levels: Health Ministry

international.h: EU leaders rally behind Ukraine
international.b: At a Brussels summit attended by Zelenskyy, top EU officials stressed keeping up arms for Ukraine and sanctions on Russia. "This is no time to withdraw support," said Antonio Costa.
international.title: EU rallies in support of Ukraine amid Trump standoff

international.h: Pakistan orders school checks after roof collapse
international.b: At least 34 students aged 13 or younger and a teacher were killed when a roof collapsed at Al-Khair school in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

international.h: Ethiopia installs interim government in Tigray
international.b: The move follows the military pushing back an uprising the TPLF launched last month. Free elections were pledged to follow.

international.h: Croatia leaders condemn pro-Nazi chants
international.b: Hajduk Split fans marched through Split chanting pro-Nazi and antisemitic slogans before Thursday's match against Ajax.

international.h: China tells Israel to stop West Bank settlements
international.b: Foreign Minister Wang Yi told Israeli President Isaac Herzog that Israel should stop and reverse its "forced establishment" of settlements, China's foreign ministry said.

international.h: Argentine students protest Milei cuts
international.b: Students at the University of Buenos Aires covered a faculty hall with banners against President Javier Milei's spending cuts and called an assembly to announce an occupation.

international.h: Iraq parliament completes al-Zaidi's cabinet
international.b: Lawmakers approved 11 remaining portfolios and three deputy prime ministers, one of them under US sanctions, completing Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi's government.

international.h: Drone strike on tanker in Romanian waters
international.b: A drone hit the chemical tanker Wine Trader about 13 nautical miles off Sulina. Five people were rescued and seven are missing. President Nicusor Dan promised "a reaction from the Romanian state."

international.h: Saudi says Iran is encouraging Houthi attacks
international.b: Saudi diplomat Rayed Krimly said Iran is encouraging the Houthi escalation. At least 19 people have been killed in more than a week of attacks, and Riyadh's King Khalid airport has been targeted 20 times this month.

international.h: Poll: Flavio Bolsonaro edges Lula before run-off
international.b: A Quaest poll has Bolsonaro at 46% to Lula's 44%, within the margin of error, ahead of Brazil's October 25 run-off.

international.h: Ethiopian forces enter Aksum as Tigray fighting grows
international.b: Ethiopian forces and allied fighters say they expanded control across Tigray and entered Aksum; a militia claims Eritrean troops retreated, which Eritrea denies.

international.h: Ex-DUP leader Donaldson jailed for 15 years
international.b: Jeffrey Donaldson, former leader of Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party, was sentenced to 15 years for child sex offences.

international.h: Somalia sets elections for 2027
international.b: Parliamentary elections are planned for April 15, 2027, followed by a presidential vote on May 15, the election commission said.

international.h: Teen dies as heavy rain floods Istanbul
international.b: A 14-year-old boy was electrocuted after stepping into a puddle in Istanbul's Fatih district as heavy rain caved in roads and snarled traffic.

international.h: Israel has detained 2,000+ Palestinian children
international.b: The Palestinian Prisoner's Society says Israel has detained more than 2,000 Palestinian children since October 2023, with at least 350 now in Israeli prisons.

international.h: Harry and Meghan make first joint UK appearances
international.b: The Duke and Duchess of Sussex visited a youth recording studio and a food bank in Nottingham, their first joint appearances since returning to the UK.

international.h: Myanmar's leader wins back neighbours
international.b: Min Aung Hlaing, whose 2021 power grab triggered a civil war, received a red-carpet welcome with an honour guard in Kuala Lumpur last week.

international.h: Sally Rooney's books pulled from UK sale
international.b: Publisher Faber said UK law bars it from passing on earnings to Rooney, who pledged them to a group the UK designates as a terrorist organization.

business.h: AI borrowing slows as debt jitters hit tech
business.b: Morgan Stanley data show debt issuance for AI projects slowed last month from a June record, and CoreWeave bonds fell sharply as stocks slumped on borrowing-cost fears.

business.h: Retail sales up 0.8%, boosted by gas spending
business.b: September retail sales beat forecasts of 0.3%, but sales rose just 0.2% excluding gas stations, where business jumped 6.4%.
The producer price index rose 6.3% in September from a year earlier and 1.3% from August, driven by fuel prices including diesel.

business.h: Virginia's Data Center Alley may be hitting a limit
business.b: Loudoun County, home to the world's highest concentration of data centers, faces questions about what happens if growth slows.
business.title: "Data Center Alley" in suburban Virginia may be hitting a dead end

science.b: ACOG updated its guidelines for the first time since 2014, recommending hormone therapy alongside antidepressants and nonhormonal options for symptoms like hot flashes and insomnia.
science.title: Hot flashes, night sweats, insomnia – OB-GYNS set new rules for menopause treatment

science.h: New type of sunscreen hits US store shelves
science.b: The first US sunscreens with BEMT, approved in June, offer broad protection without white streaking and have decades of safety data, dermatologists say.

sports.b: Wil Lutz's field goal won it after a Sam Darnold interception. Analyst Ryan Fitzpatrick ripped Bo Nix, who threw for 107 yards.

sports.h: Brewers sweep Dodgers, reach World Series
sports.b: Milwaukee won Game 4 6-4 to complete the NLCS sweep. Jake Bauers, with six RBI in the series, was named NLCS MVP.
FIFA president Gianni Infantino apologized over this year's World Cup controversies, but European delegates said "no satisfactory answers were provided."

sports.h: Caleb Williams pushes back on injury reports
sports.b: The Bears quarterback is on track for a possible Week 6 return from his hamstring injury but said he still doesn't know if he'll play Sunday against Atlanta.

sports.h: Josh Jacobs sues to block release of video
sports.b: The Packers running back filed suit against a Wisconsin police department to keep evidence from his criminal case, including an alleged video, from being released.

sports.h: Eagles rule out Jalen Hurts with blood clot
sports.b: A follow-up ultrasound found movement in a blood clot in Hurts' calf, so he will miss Sunday's game against Carolina.
Milwaukee rallied after Blake Snell was left in for the seventh inning, pushing the Dodgers to the brink of elimination.

sports.h: Real Madrid edges Roma 4-3 in Mourinho return
sports.b: Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid rallied for a late 4-3 Champions League win at Roma, while PSG routed Manchester City.

sports.h: ALCS Game 3 moved to 1 p.m. for rain
sports.b: MLB moved Thursday's Rays-Guardians Game 3 in Cleveland up from 6 p.m. to 1 p.m. ET because of forecast rain; the series is tied 1-1.

goodnews.b: A family of barn owls nested in a water tower near Central Park, the first documented barn owl nest in Manhattan in modern history, drawing nightly crowds.

local.h: Pfizer Building fix: 1/64th of an inch at a time
local.b: Engineering plans for the city's largest office-to-housing conversion show crews will jack sagging floors up about 7 inches in tiny increments.
local.title: Inside the plan to fix the nearly collapsed Pfizer Building, 1/64th of an inch at a time

local.h: Storms, wind and chill hit NYC weather
local.b: Temperatures drop from near 80 Thursday to the 50s by Saturday, with potentially dangerous storms Friday evening, the NWS says.
local.title: NYC’s whiplash weather continues into weekend with heavy winds, chilly temps, NWS says

local.h: Mamdani urges parking lots to ban ICE
local.b: The mayor and more than 100 elected officials asked lot and garage owners not to make their property available to ICE as a staging ground.
local.title: Mamdani and 100+ NY officials urge parking lot owners to ban ICE

local.b: A city comptroller's report found EMS teams are taking longer to reach people even as life-threatening emergencies rise.
local.title: NYC ambulance response times have grown 41% as life-threatening calls rise

local.h: Judge tosses Trump suit over NYC sanctuary laws
local.b: A federal judge dismissed the administration's lawsuit challenging the city's limits on cooperating with immigration authorities.
local.title: Federal judge tosses Trump administration lawsuit challenging NYC sanctuary laws

local.h: 2 charged in fentanyl death of NYC college student
local.b: Federal prosecutors unsealed an indictment over the fatal fentanyl poisoning and alleged rape of a student and the near-fatal poisoning of another at a Manhattan residence hall.
local.title: 2 men charged in fatal fentanyl poisoning of NYC college student, alleged rape

local.h: Street homelessness spending tripled, and so did need
local.b: The state comptroller found NYC spending on street homelessness and related 311 calls both tripled since 2019.
local.title: NYC spending on homelessness has soared. So has the number of people on the street.

local.h: Citi Bike expands into seven more neighborhoods
local.b: The bike-share network finished adding docks in areas including parts of the North Bronx and eastern Brooklyn, the city said.
local.title: Citi Bike finishes expansion into 7 areas, including parts of North Bronx, Eastern Brooklyn

local.h: Comptroller backs off pension investment in Israel bonds
local.b: NYC Comptroller Mark Levine said he won't invest city pension funds in Israel bonds.
local.title: Early Addition: NYC comptroller backs off investing city pension funds in Israel bonds

local.b: Police charged Francis Cabello, 32, with murder in the death of her daughter Fabiana in Richmond Hill, a day after she called 911.
local.title: Queens mother charged with murder in death of 5-year-old daughter, NYPD says

periods.name: Tonight
periods.text: Showers and possibly a thunderstorm before 11pm, then a slight chance of showers between 11pm and 2am, then a chance of rain after 2am.  Low around 50. Breezy, with a northwest wind 14 to 23 mph.  Chance of precipitation is 80%. New precipitation amounts between a tenth and quarter of an inch, except higher amounts possible in thunderstorms.

periods.name: Saturday
periods.text: A 30 percent chance of rain, mainly before 8am.  Cloudy, then gradually becoming mostly sunny, with a temperature falling to around 50 by 11am. Breezy, with a north wind around 22 mph.

periods.name: Saturday Night
periods.text: Mostly clear, with a low around 42. North wind around 16 mph.

periods.name: Sunday
periods.text: Sunny, with a high near 54. Northeast wind 8 to 11 mph.

periods.name: Sunday Night
periods.text: Mostly clear, with a low around 46.

periods.name: Monday
periods.text: Mostly sunny, with a high near 58.
